source.candidate_scope: test-only exact Q24/KV4/D256/RoPE64 full-attention preprocess warp-local RMS reduction

topology.ownership: one CTA per Q or K head per token

candidate.mechanism: Warp 0 reconstructs the production 256-thread square-sum tree locally: scalar 128, 64, and 32 pairings followed by shuffle-down 16, 8, 4, 2, and 1. Lane 0 publishes one FP32 inverse RMS through shared memory; all 256 threads retain the centered RMSNorm, BF16-RNE boundary, in-place key behavior, and post-normalization RoPE order.

exact_fixtures.query_output: bitwise exact against production and the decomposed reference
exact_fixtures.in_place_key_output: bitwise exact against production and the decomposed reference
exact_fixtures.raw_gate_output: bitwise exact against production and the decomposed reference

resources_and_static_mechanism.interpretation: The intended shared-tree-to-warp-local mechanism compiled: eight CTA barrier points and 1,020 static shared bytes disappeared without reducing six-CTA/SM occupancy. Static evidence does not establish a useful Decode latency gain.

profile_headroom_context.claim_boundary: The raw production-kernel time is directional headroom context from a preceding Nsys capture, not this candidate's end-to-end saving.

benchmark_protocol.comparison: production shared-tree kernel versus test-only warp-RMS kernel in one binary, process, stream, and deterministic synthetic fixture
benchmark_protocol.paired_statistic: median of five per-round values; each round pairs the mean of its two production passes with the mean of its two candidate passes
benchmark_protocol.in_place_key_timing_interpretation: Both routes perform the same in-place key transformation count in each timed pass, which is sufficient for a rejection almost eight times below the absolute gate. Any future promotion-quality rerun must reset both key buffers to the same seed before every pass.
benchmark_protocol.stop_loss: Stop after process 1 and skip production integration, whole-model timing, and candidate Nsys when the authoritative M1 cell misses any frozen Decode selection gate.

stop_loss.reason: The authoritative M1 median reaches only 1.03734x and 0.000158074 ms/call, projecting 0.00252919 ms/token over 16 layers. It misses the frozen 1.10x, 0.00125-ms/call, and 0.020-ms/token gates despite positive supporting cells.
stop_loss.decision: reject production promotion of this exact warp-RMS mapping and retain production

validation.formal_process_1_exit_interpretation: expected frozen performance-gate rejection; the two failed assertions are the M1 selection gate and the combined summary gate after correctness, resource, Graph, invalid-call, and supporting-cell gates passed

next_priority.reason: The preprocess cell's measured 0.00252919-ms/token projection is immaterial against the remaining 7.314-ms/token gap. Return to a bounded Decode projection cell with materially larger raw-time leverage; Prefill remains deferred until the Decode stage target is met.

claim_limits: This rejection applies to the exact one-warp RMS construction inside the fixed Q24/KV4/D256/RoPE64 preprocess topology, not every preprocess optimization or fusion topology.
The 0.00252919-ms/token value is an isolated synthetic 16-layer projection, not a whole-model measurement.
Graph evidence proves a distinct one-node kernel, expected topology, successful instantiation, and successful replay; replay outputs were not separately compared bitwise.

The timing harness did not reset the in-place key buffers between timed passes. Both routes execute equal transformation counts, so this does not rescue a candidate 7.91 times below the frozen absolute gate, but promotion would require per-pass reset.
Resource queries cover registers, static shared memory, local memory, maximum threads, and active CTAs/SM; stack bytes were not queried and no zero-stack claim is made.
Finite and nonfinite M1/M2/M8/M16 fixtures provide strong bitwise evidence but are not an exhaustive enumeration of every reduction-tree slot or BF16 pattern.
M2, M8, and M16 are supporting cells; their positive results do not override failure of the authoritative Decode M1 gate or begin Prefill optimization.
No process 2, production integration, whole-model end-to-end benchmark, or candidate Nsys capture was run after first-process stop-loss.
Production, the 107.314000-ms/token anchor, the serial one-stream schedule, and Prefill state remain unchanged.
